# Remove-ZbxUser

## SYNOPSIS

Removes users.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxUser [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A user is an account that logs in to the frontend or the API, with its role, its user groups and the media it is notified on. The Remove-ZbxUser cmdlet deletes the users given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with user.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a user by name

```powershell
Remove-ZbxUser -InputObject 'jdoe' -Confirm:$false
```

-InputObject takes a username, an id or a user object. ConfirmImpact is High, so PowerShell asks first unless -Confirm:$false is given. A user still named in an action's operations cannot be deleted (the API refuses).

### Example 2: Delete every member of a user group, through the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxUser -UserGroup 'Operators' | Remove-ZbxUser -WhatIf
Get-ZbxUser -UserGroup 'Operators' | Remove-ZbxUser -Confirm:$false
Get-ZbxUser -UserGroup 'Operators' -CountOutput
```

Get-ZbxUser -UserGroup writes the group's users; Remove-ZbxUser binds each one and deletes them in one call. Run it with -WhatIf first to see what would go.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
